Many will reappear in the stories of ⟦p:saul_2478|Saul⟧ and ⟦p:david_994|David⟧. The chapter ends with a note of failure: Judah could not drive out the ⟦p:jebusite_748|Jebusites⟧ from ⟦l:jerusalem_636|Jerusalem⟧.
16:
After ⟦l:judah_1280|Judah⟧ in the south, the lot falls to the descendants of ⟦p:joseph_1710|Joseph⟧, the two tribes of ⟦l:ephraim-territory_1292|Ephraim⟧ and ⟦p:manasseh_1928|Manasseh⟧, who receive the heart of the country, the central hill country north of ⟦l:jerusalem_636|Jerusalem⟧. This chapter sets out their shared southern boundary, running from the ⟦l:jordan_653|Jordan⟧ near ⟦l:jericho_634|Jericho⟧ up into the hills past ⟦l:bethel_202|Bethel⟧, and down westward to ⟦l:gezer_463|Gezer⟧ and the sea.

Then it turns to ⟦l:ephraim-territory_1292|Ephraim⟧, ⟦p:joseph_1710|Joseph⟧'s younger son, whom ⟦p:israel_682|Jacob⟧ had blessed ahead of his elder brother. Ephraim's territory is the southern part of the Joseph lands, a fertile hill region that will become the centre of the northern kingdom in later centuries. So central will the tribe become that the prophets sometimes use the name Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom of Israel.

The chapter is short, and it ends with a sentence that is becoming a refrain. The Ephraimites did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in ⟦l:gezer_463|Gezer⟧, but made them forced labourers. The work of taking the land is still unfinished.
17:
⟦p:ephraim_1206|Ephraim⟧'s allotment has been described, and now it is the turn of ⟦p:manasseh_1928|Manasseh⟧, the elder son of ⟦p:joseph_1710|Joseph⟧. Half of the tribe, the descendants of Manasseh's son ⟦p:machir_1877|Machir⟧, have already settled east of the ⟦l:jordan_653|Jordan⟧ in ⟦p:gilead_1317|Gilead⟧ and ⟦l:bashan_159|Bashan⟧. The rest receive land west of the river, north of Ephraim, stretching toward the plain of Jezreel and the coast.

Here the five daughters of ⟦p:zelophehad_3035|Zelophehad⟧ reappear. Their father had died without sons, and in the wilderness they had come before ⟦p:moses_2108|Moses⟧ to ask that his name and inheritance not be lost. Moses had brought their case to the Lord, and the Lord had agreed. Now Mahlah, ⟦p:noah_2211|Noah⟧, Hoglah, Milcah and ⟦p:tirzah_2868|Tirzah⟧ come before ⟦p:eleazar_1062|Eleazar⟧ and ⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧ to claim what was promised.

The chapter ends with a complaint. The tribes of ⟦p:joseph_1710|Joseph⟧ say they are too numerous for the land they have been given. The real difficulty soon comes out: the open valleys are held by Canaanites with iron chariots, especially around ⟦l:beth-shean_233|Beth-shean⟧ and the ⟦l:valley_of_jezreel_1211|Valley of Jezreel⟧. ⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧'s reply is practical and direct, and it is addressed to people who have more strength than they think.
18:
The scene shifts. Until now the camp has been at ⟦l:gilgal_476|Gilgal⟧, near the ⟦l:jordan_653|Jordan⟧. Now the whole congregation gathers at ⟦l:shiloh_1081|Shiloh⟧, in the hill country of ⟦p:ephraim_1206|Ephraim⟧, and sets up the Tent of Meeting there, the portable sanctuary built in the wilderness under ⟦p:moses_2108|Moses⟧. Shiloh will remain Israel's central place of worship for generations, and it is there, much later, that the boy ⟦p:samuel_2469|Samuel⟧ will grow up.

⟦l:judah_1280|Judah⟧ and the tribes of ⟦p:joseph_1710|Joseph⟧ have received their land, but seven tribes have not, and they seem in no hurry. ⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧'s question to them is pointed: how long will you put off taking possession of the land the Lord has given you? He organises a survey. Three men from each of the seven tribes go out through the country and write a description of it, town by town, in seven portions. Then lots are cast before the Lord at ⟦l:shiloh_1081|Shiloh⟧.

The first lot falls to ⟦l:benjamin-territory_1293|Benjamin⟧, the tribe descended from ⟦p:israel_682|Jacob⟧'s youngest son. Its territory is small but strategic, a strip of land between ⟦l:judah_1280|Judah⟧ and ⟦p:ephraim_1206|Ephraim⟧ that includes ⟦l:jericho_634|Jericho⟧, ⟦l:bethel_202|Bethel⟧, ⟦l:gibeon_470|Gibeon⟧ and ⟦l:jebus_629|Jebus⟧, the town better known as ⟦l:jerusalem_636|Jerusalem⟧. From this little tribe, Israel's first king will one day come.
19:
The lots are still being cast at ⟦l:shiloh_1081|Shiloh⟧, and this chapter completes the distribution with the remaining six tribes. Each receives its portion in turn.

⟦p:simeon_2741|Simeon⟧'s inheritance lies inside ⟦l:judah_1280|Judah⟧'s territory in the south, around ⟦l:beersheba_170|Beersheba⟧, because Judah's share was more than it needed. Then the lots move north, to the hills and valleys of ⟦l:galilee_433|Galilee⟧. ⟦p:zebulun_3002|Zebulun⟧, ⟦p:issachar_645|Issachar⟧, ⟦p:asher_337|Asher⟧ and ⟦p:naphtali_2149|Naphtali⟧ settle the lands around the Valley of ⟦l:jezreel_643|Jezreel⟧, the coast north of Mount ⟦l:carmel_278|Carmel⟧, and the hills west of the ⟦l:sea_of_galilee_1032|Sea of Galilee⟧.

The last lot falls to ⟦p:dan_973|Dan⟧, whose territory lies on the western slopes and coastal plain near ⟦l:joppa_652|Joppa⟧. A brief note looks ahead: the Danites will lose this land and migrate to the far north, a story told at length near the end of Judges.

Then comes a touching close. When everyone else has received an inheritance, the Israelites give one to ⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧ himself, the town he asks for, ⟦l:timnath-serah_1167|Timnath-serah⟧ in the hill country of ⟦l:ephraim-territory_1292|Ephraim⟧. The leader is served last.
20:
The land has been divided, and now two kinds of special towns are set apart within it. The first are the cities of refuge, which ⟦p:moses_2108|Moses⟧ had commanded in the wilderness.

In the ancient world, a killing usually brought a duty of vengeance. A close relative of the dead, called the avenger of blood, was expected to pursue the killer, whether the death was murder or an accident. These six cities give someone who has killed unintentionally a place to flee and be safe until the case is heard before the community. If the killing was accidental, the person may stay there, protected, until the death of the high priest, and then return home.

The cities are spread out so that one is always within reach: three west of the ⟦l:jordan_653|Jordan⟧, ⟦l:kedesh_676|Kedesh⟧ in the north, ⟦l:shechem_1069|Shechem⟧ in the centre and ⟦l:hebron_551|Hebron⟧ in the south, and three to the east, ⟦l:bezer_247|Bezer⟧, ⟦l:ramoth_983|Ramoth in Gilead⟧ and ⟦l:golan_486|Golan⟧. Notably, the protection extends to foreigners living among Israel as well. After the long years of war, the book pauses here over the ordinary workings of justice in a settled land.
21:
The cities of refuge have been named. Now the leaders of the Levites come to ⟦l:shiloh_1081|Shiloh⟧ to remind ⟦p:eleazar_1062|Eleazar⟧ and ⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧ of another promise from ⟦p:moses_2108|Moses⟧. The Levites have no territory of their own, but they were to be given towns to live in, with pastureland for their animals.

This chapter lists forty-eight of these Levitical towns, scattered through every tribe. They are distributed by lot among the three clans descended from ⟦p:levi_1820|Levi⟧'s sons, ⟦p:kohath_1790|Kohath⟧, ⟦p:gershon_1305|Gershon⟧ and ⟦p:merari_2004|Merari⟧, with the priests, the descendants of ⟦p:aaron_1|Aaron⟧, receiving their towns in ⟦l:judah_1280|Judah⟧, ⟦p:simeon_2741|Simeon⟧ and ⟦p:benjamin_463|Benjamin⟧. The result is that the tribe set apart for God's service lives among all the others, rather than in one corner of the land. Among the towns given to the priests is ⟦l:anathoth_63|Anathoth⟧, which centuries later will be the home of the prophet ⟦p:jeremiah_853|Jeremiah⟧.

The list ends with a short, ringing summary that gathers up the whole first part of the story. The Lord gave Israel all the land he had sworn to their fathers, he gave them rest on every side, and not one of all his good promises had failed.
22:
The land is divided and the fighting is over, and ⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧ now keeps faith with the eastern tribes. ⟦p:reuben_2429|Reuben⟧, ⟦p:gad_1262|Gad⟧ and half of ⟦p:manasseh_1928|Manasseh⟧ have fought alongside their brothers for years, as they promised at the very beginning. Joshua commends them, blesses them, and sends them home across the ⟦l:jordan_653|Jordan⟧ with a share of the plunder.

But on their way, at the edge of the river, they build a great altar. To the tribes west of the ⟦l:jordan_653|Jordan⟧, this looks like the beginning of rebellion. The law allowed sacrifice only at the one altar before the tabernacle, and the memory of what unfaithfulness had cost the nation was still fresh, both at ⟦l:peor_933|Peor⟧ in the wilderness and in the sin of ⟦p:achan_61|Achan⟧. The whole congregation gathers at ⟦l:shiloh_1081|Shiloh⟧, ready for war.

Instead of attacking, they send a delegation: ⟦p:phinehas_2349|Phinehas⟧ the priest, the son of ⟦p:eleazar_1062|Eleazar⟧, with ten leaders, one from each tribe. Phinehas was known for his zeal at ⟦l:peor_933|Peor⟧, where his action had stopped a plague. The confrontation that follows on the far side of the ⟦l:jordan_653|Jordan⟧ turns on whether a river will divide God's people, and on how a misunderstanding can be handled before it becomes a civil war.
23:
A long time has passed. Israel has rest from its enemies, and ⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧ is now very old. Knowing that he will soon die, he calls together the leaders of Israel, the elders, heads, judges and officers. The place is not named.

What follows is a farewell speech, the kind that ⟦p:moses_2108|Moses⟧ gave at the end of his life in Deuteronomy, and it is full of echoes of that book. ⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧ looks back on what the Lord has done, fighting for Israel. He looks around at the nations that still remain in the land. And he looks ahead with a clear warning about what will happen if Israel begins to mix with those nations, intermarrying with them and calling on their gods.

The tone is both grateful and grave. ⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧ repeats the summary heard at the end of chapter twenty-one, that not one of the Lord's good promises has failed. But he adds its shadow. The same faithfulness that kept every good promise will also keep every warning. With this speech, the old soldier hands over to the leaders the responsibility he has carried since ⟦p:moses_2108|Moses⟧ died.
24:
For his final act, ⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧ gathers all the tribes of Israel at ⟦l:shechem_1069|Shechem⟧. The place is full of memory. It was here that ⟦p:abraham_58|Abraham⟧ first built an altar in the land of ⟦p:canaan_914|Canaan⟧, and here that ⟦p:israel_682|Jacob⟧ buried the foreign gods of his household under an oak. Here too, earlier in this book, the people heard the law read between the mountains of Ebal and Gerizim.

⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧ speaks in the name of the Lord, and he tells Israel's story from the beginning: ⟦p:abraham_58|Abraham⟧'s family serving other gods beyond the ⟦l:euphrates_421|Euphrates⟧, the patriarchs, the slavery in ⟦l:egypt_362|Egypt⟧, the exodus, the wilderness, and the gift of a land they did not toil for. Then he sets a choice before the people, and declares his own.

The exchange that follows has the shape of a covenant ceremony, with words spoken, written down and witnessed by a great stone beneath an oak near the sanctuary. ⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧ presses the people hard and will not accept an easy answer.

The book then ends with three burials. ⟦p:joshua_1727|Joshua⟧ dies at a hundred and ten and is buried in his own town. The bones of ⟦p:joseph_1710|Joseph⟧, carried out of ⟦l:egypt_362|Egypt⟧ as he asked at the end of Genesis, are laid to rest at ⟦l:shechem_1069|Shechem⟧, on the land ⟦p:israel_682|Jacob⟧ bought. And ⟦p:eleazar_1062|Eleazar⟧ the priest, son of ⟦p:aaron_1|Aaron⟧, is buried in the hill country of ⟦p:ephraim_1206|Ephraim⟧. With them a generation passes.
